title: Lesson 7 · The Adverb
blurb: Finding adverbs; how/when/where/how much; what they modify; adverbial clauses; adverb mistakes.

items.prompt:
Which word is the adverb?

“That vessel sails slowly.”
items.explain: “slowly” tells how it sails — it modifies the verb, so it is the adverb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the adverb?

“He built a house there.”
items.explain: “there” tells where — the adverb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the adverb?

“Emma is quite late.”
items.explain: “quite” tells how much — it modifies “late,” so it is the adverb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the adverb?

“Those mountains are very high.”
items.explain: “very” tells how much — it modifies “high,” so it is the adverb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the adverb?

“I will shortly return.”
items.explain: “shortly” tells when — the adverb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the adverb?

“You will never see him.”
items.explain: “never” tells when (not at any time) — the adverb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the adverb?

“She sang here.”
items.explain: “here” tells where — the adverb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the adverb?

“He afterwards escaped.”
items.explain: “afterwards” tells when — the adverb.

items.prompt:
Does this adverb tell how, when, where, or how much?

“slowly”
items.explain: “slowly” tells how — the manner.

items.prompt:
Does this adverb tell how, when, where, or how much?

“yesterday”
items.explain: “yesterday” tells when — the time.

items.prompt:
Does this adverb tell how, when, where, or how much?

“there”
items.explain: “there” tells where — the place.

items.prompt:
Does this adverb tell how, when, where, or how much?

“very”
items.explain: “very” tells how much — the degree.

items.prompt:
Does this adverb tell how, when, where, or how much?

“gently”
items.explain: “gently” tells how — the manner.

items.prompt:
Does this adverb tell how, when, where, or how much?

“soon”
items.explain: “soon” tells when — the time.

items.prompt:
Does this adverb tell how, when, where, or how much?

“here”
items.explain: “here” tells where — the place.

items.prompt:
Does this adverb tell how, when, where, or how much?

“quite”
items.explain: “quite” tells how much — the degree.

items.prompt:
What does the adverb “sweetly” modify?

“Birds sing sweetly.”
items.explain: “sweetly” tells how the birds sing — it modifies the verb “sing.”

items.prompt:
What does the adverb “very” modify?

“Very large vessels sailed.”
items.explain: “very” modifies the adjective “large.”

items.prompt:
What does the adverb “quite” modify?

“He rode quite fast.”
items.explain: “quite” modifies the adverb “fast.”

items.prompt:
What does the adverb “softly” modify?

“She spoke softly.”
items.explain: “softly” tells how she spoke — it modifies the verb “spoke.”

items.prompt:
What does the adverb “too” modify?

“The soup is too hot.”
items.explain: “too” modifies the adjective “hot.”

items.prompt:
What does the adverb “very” modify?

“They left very quickly.”
items.explain: “very” modifies the adverb “quickly.”

items.prompt:
Which words are the adverbial clause (they tell how, when, where, or why)?

“Birds sing when day breaks.”
items.explain: “when day breaks” tells when they sing — the adverbial clause.

items.prompt:
Which words are the adverbial clause (they tell how, when, where, or why)?

“Stay here until I return.”
items.explain: “until I return” tells when to stay — the adverbial clause.

items.prompt:
Which words are the adverbial clause (they tell how, when, where, or why)?

“We rested because we were tired.”
items.explain: “because we were tired” tells why we rested — the adverbial clause.

items.prompt:
Which words are the adverbial clause (they tell how, when, where, or why)?

“Call me if you need help.”
items.explain: “if you need help” tells the condition — the adverbial clause.

items.prompt:
Which words are the adverbial clause (they tell how, when, where, or why)?

“He smiled while she spoke.”
items.explain: “while she spoke” tells when he smiled — the adverbial clause.

items.prompt:
Which words are the adverbial clause (they tell how, when, where, or why)?

“Plants grow where it is warm.”
items.explain: “where it is warm” tells where they grow — the adverbial clause.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word:

“I don’t want ___ today.”
items.explain: Avoid two negatives: “don’t want anything.”

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word:

“Samuel speaks very ___.”
items.explain: Use an -ly adverb to tell how he speaks: distinctly.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word:

“This flower smells ___.”
items.explain: After “smells,” use an adjective: smells sweet.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word:

“You ought to read ___.”
items.explain: Use an adverb to tell how to read: more slowly.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word:

“The team played ___.”
items.explain: Use “well,” the adverb, to tell how they played.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word:

“Don’t tell ___.”
items.explain: Avoid two negatives: “Don’t tell anybody.”

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word:

“The country looks ___.”
items.explain: After “looks,” use an adjective: looks beautiful.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word:

“Drive ___ on the ice.”
items.explain: Use an -ly adverb to tell how to drive: safely.
